subject: Edge peering impact on private deployment SLA — exception request
body:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@haelix.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed edge peering

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick intro. We're excited to be getting Redwood Private set up for our inference fleet, but during our last two weeks of testing we observed intermittent tail latency spikes that appear to coincide with maintenance windows on our colo edge routers and on a third-party peering fabric. Because those segments are managed entirely by our network team (they own the SD-WAN and last-mile peering), we wanted to request an SLA exception for those customer-controlled network tails and discuss how Redwood would attribute latency/availability when the root cause maps to our peering fabric.

Quick context:
- Observed periodic p95 spikes from 40ms to 320ms between our edge and the Redwood ingress during peering flap events.
- The infra in question is in our colocated POPs; Haelix manages routing and BGP sessions there (we control the ASN and BGP filters).
- We need an explicit carveout so our SREs can operate without triggering Redwood SLA remediation or credits for incidents that are outside Redwood's control.

Can you advise what evidence Redwood would need to accept a formal carveout and how the SLA language would read for a private deployment with customer-managed peering? I can attach peering logs and a simplified network diagram.

Best,
Alice Chen
SR Mgr, Infrastructure — Haelix AI
Attachments: haelix-peering-events.csv (CSV of timestamps, AS path, event tags)

---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@haelix.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed edge peering

Hi Alice — thanks for the note and the sample CSV. I'm looping in Marcus (infra runtime) and Karthik (contracts/ops) so we can align on a practical carveout that protects both sides. Initial thoughts:

- We can define a "Customer-Controlled Network Segment" (CCNS) in the SLA appendix, limited to colo racks and peering fabric under Haelix ASN that you manage.
- For attribution, Redwood will require timestamped traceroutes, BGP session logs, and request-level traces (we'll correlate your timestamps with our ingress logs).
- If an incident is attributable to the CCNS by the evidence above, Redwood will exclude that window from SLA uptime/latency calculations.

Could you send a simple network diagram and one week of representative p50/p95/p99 telemetry? That will let us draft the carveout language. Marcus — can you propose a short list of acceptable evidence formats and an operational playbook for attribution?

I'll follow up with a draft amendment once we have those artifacts.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Principal Account Manager
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@haelix.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed edge peering

Hi — adding the technical detail Priya asked for. For the purposes of a clean carveout and reproducible attribution we recommend the following minimal evidence bundle: 

1) BGP session history showing route changes and up/down timestamps (format: MRT or CSV export).
2) Traceroute matrix from a representative set of Haelix edge peers to our ingress IPs for the incident window (ICMP/TCP-based traces stamped with epoch ms).
3) Packet loss and jitter telemetry from your SD-WAN controller or colo SRs (one-minute granularity preferred).
4) Request-level ingress logs from your side with request_id or timestamp that we can match to Redwood ingress logs.

Operational notes:
- We'll run an initial correlation analysis within 24 business hours of receiving the evidence and provide a provisional attribution report.
- If attribution is inconclusive, we'll open a joint triage bridge; if evidence clearly points to the customer-controlled segment, Redwood will mark the interval as excluded from SLA computations.

I've attached a short definition draft for the carveout terms so legal can iterate: proposed-carveout-terminology.pdf

—Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@haelix.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed edge peering

Thanks Marcus and Priya — this is helpful. We've exported the traceroutes and BGP session logs for the last 30 days and attached a current network diagram. You'll find the haelix-peering-events.csv in the first email and the new diagram attached.

Quick answers to a couple points:
- We can provide per-request timestamps (our proxy adds request_id headers) — we'll redact customer PII before sharing.
- We accept a carveout that excludes intervals where primary evidence points to our edge or third-party peering fabric.
- We do want the SLA language to still require Redwood to maintain core ingress capacity and post-incident remediation on your side (i.e., if the same incident involves a failure in Redwood's ingress, that portion remains your responsibility).

Please find attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf, haelix-peering-events.csv (re-attached)

Best,
Alice

---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@haelix.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed edge peering

Alice — thanks for turning those artifacts around quickly. Next steps and owners: 

1) Redwood will draft a one-page amendment (SLA Appendix A: Customer-Controlled Network Segment) that includes: clear definition of the CCNS, the evidence bundle required for attribution, and the exclusion mechanics (how excluded intervals are removed from uptime/latency calculations). Owner: Priya/Contracts.
2) Marcus will produce an internal triage checklist and a short example attribution report to show how we correlate traces. Owner: Marcus/Infra.
3) Legal (Evelyn) and Ops (Karthik) will review the language and confirm there are no unexpected liability gaps. Owner: Evelyn/Karthik.
4) We will include a fallback policy: if customer evidence is incomplete, Redwood will provisionally treat the interval as included in the SLA for the purposes of credits, but will offer a joint investigation credit mitigation if the investigation proves customer attribution within 30 days.

I've attached a draft amendment for initial review: redwood-amendment-draft.docx. Please review and flag any edits in the doc (track changes appreciated). If this looks okay, we'll prepare a single-signature amendment and fold it into the existing redlines for DEAL-HAE-8731.

Could we target a signed amendment by Oct 14 so we can lock the SLA language before go-live?

Thanks all — copying Evelyn so legal can triage.

—Priya
Principal Account Manager
Redwood Inference
